title: Senior's toolkit: Python at work
summary: uv, pytest's everyday flags, mypy, pdb and ruff: the commands an experienced Python developer types daily.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: Python at work
steps.body: The commands behind a healthy Python repo: set it up, test it fast, find the bug, keep it clean.

toolkit.what: Install exactly what `uv.lock` says into `.venv`. In CI it fails if the lock is out of date with `pyproject.toml`.
flags: fail instead of updating the lock
use the lock as is, do not check it
toolkit.when: first step of every CI job and Dockerfile

toolkit.what: Add a dependency (updates `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.venv`), or run a command inside the project's environment.
toolkit.example:
uv add --dev mypy ruff
uv run mypy --strict src

toolkit.what: The fast debugging loop: rerun only what failed, stop at the first failure, show full diffs.
flags: only the tests that failed last time
open the debugger at the failure
toolkit.when: a test is red and you are fixing it

toolkit.what: Type check the code. `--strict` is what most teams use for new code.
flags: annotations required, no implicit Any, None checked
silence one line, with the code, and a comment why

toolkit.what: Development mode: shows ResourceWarnings (unclosed files), asyncio debug checks, and warnings that are normally hidden.
flags: stop in the debugger at an uncaught exception

toolkit.what: Lint and format in one fast tool (replaces flake8, isort and black for most teams).
flags: CI: fail if a file is not formatted
toolkit.example: uv run ruff check --fix . && uv run ruff format .

steps.prompt: Match the flag to the situation.
pairs: rerun only what failed a minute ago
CI must install exactly the tested versions
find a file that is never closed
require annotations and handle every None
inspect variables at the failing assert

steps.prompt: CI fails: `error: The lockfile at uv.lock needs to be updated, but --locked was provided`. What happened?
options: Someone changed the dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and did not commit the updated `uv.lock`
`--locked` must not be used in CI
steps.explain: That is `--locked` doing its job. Run `uv lock` (or `uv add`, which updates both) locally and commit `uv.lock`.

steps.prompt: Rerun only the failed tests whose names contain `refund`, stopping at the first failure.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Put the loop in muscle memory: `uv sync`, edit, `pytest -x --lf`, `mypy --strict`, `ruff check --fix`, commit. Run the same four commands in CI, in the same order, so "works on my machine" and "passes in CI" mean the same thing.
